newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Benetton 1996 net profit up, cash mounts.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Benetton 1996 net profit up, cash mounts.

text.p: Italian clothing group Benetton boosted its 1996 net profit 11.5 percent and said Thursday it intended to raise its dividend by 18 percent.
Analysts said the results were fairly in line with forecasts but they foresaw a slowdown in net profit growth in 1997.

Benetton's consolidated net profit rose to a record 246 billion lire ($148.7 million) from 220 billion ($133 million in 1995, and it said it would pay a dividend on ordinary shares of 500 lire (30 cents), up from 425 (26 cents) previously.

Revnues were 2.87 trillion lire ($1.73 billion), down from 2.94 trillion ($1.77 billion) in 1995. The group noted the effect of marked appreciation of the lira against major currencies and pointed out it had also sold off some non-strategic operations.
Sales around the globe had grown 4 percent with steady growth in European markets and the Middle East.
As far as 1997 was concerned, analysts said the group was likely to see net profits grow at a slower pace than in 1996.

"In 1997 I expect them to make more or less the same -- maybe two to three percent more in terms of sales...and with a net profit of a maximum five to six percent higher," said one British investment house analyst.
